story: This night-time image was taken at ESO's Astronomical Site Monitor on Cerro Armazones, a mountain in the Chilean desert close to Paranal Observatory, home of the Very Large Telescope.

When this picture was released, Cerro Armazones was one of about half a dozen candidate sites for the Extremely Large Telescope, or ELT. With a mirror in the 40-metre class, the ELT was described as set to become the world's biggest eye on the sky.

Choosing a site for a telescope like that is a careful process. An ELT Site Selection Advisory Committee reviewed the options, and Cerro Armazones came out as its recommended site on the final shortlist. The committee gave two reasons for its choice: the mountain's excellent sky quality, and the fact that its operation could be integrated with the existing observatory at nearby Paranal. Being close to an established site means the two can share operations rather than starting from scratch.
